_schema.description: Curated geopolitical event registry per docs/019_Geopolitical_Intelligence.md. Every event must carry sources (invariant: no unverified data). severity and oil_supply_impact are 0-10; confidence is 0-1. status: active | monitoring | resolved. Resolved events are kept forever (invariant: historical information must remain preserved).

events.description: Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz on 2026-02-28 following the US/Israel air campaign. Partially reopened in early July 2026 after a US-Iran memorandum of understanding and indirect talks in Qatar, then re-closed on 2026-07-13 amid renewed missile exchanges. Approximately 25% of seaborne oil trade and 20% of global LNG transits this chokepoint.

Active military conflict between the US/Israel and Iran since late February 2026, including ongoing missile exchanges as of mid-July 2026. Drives the Hormuz closure and poses direct risk to Gulf production, export terminals, and shipping.

US-Iran indirect negotiations in Qatar produced a memorandum of understanding that briefly reopened Hormuz in early July 2026. Talks remain the primary de-escalation path; headlines around them whipsaw prices in both directions.
